heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, synchronized audio-video creation, and multimodal visual production.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a dark control-room hero with a layered, premium dashboard composition: headline and proof stack centered-left over a mesh-gradient field, while the right side is occupied by a stacked product preview shell showing Seedream UI above a Seedance motion tile. Keep the hero unexpected by using a background-overlay layout rather than a standard split. Add subtle orange glow orbs, fine grid lines, and hard-shadow cards to reinforce the operational-dashboard feel. CTA should be a solid orange pill with high contrast, and the video visual should be a preview card rather than autoplay to preserve polish and performance.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is split, content-first with a right-side product visualization to match warm traffic continuity.
Trust is a dedicated logo band immediately after hero because logos are the strongest proof signal.
Products use an alternating spotlight-plus-grid rhythm instead of a generic stacked SaaS layout.
Testimonials are condensed into a carousel to preserve density without repeating the same card pattern.
Pricing is presented as a comparison-led decision block, not a standard price table.
Final CTA is isolated as a conversion close with higher visual contrast than preceding sections.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for creative directors, video producers, art directors, and marketing teams.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark control-room paneling with subtle orange edge glow and layered product preview shell
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the headline direct and content-first, with a premium product visualization on the right showing image and video generation outputs side by side. Primary CTA button text must be 'Get started' and appear immediately in the hero. Use a concise subheadline that speaks directly to creative professionals. Visual dominance = hero-product, but the text remains highly readable.

Place recognisable logo proof immediately after the hero as the first trust anchor. Use a horizontal marquee of 3–6 logos if available; if not, substitute a metric strip. Keep it compact, high contrast, and enterprise-coded so it feels like operational validation rather than decorative social proof.

Combine the two product blocks into an alternating two-phase section. First spotlight Seedream 4.5 with a preview panel and a dense grid of its 5 capabilities; then switch background tone and mirror the layout for Seedance 1.5 Pro with motion-focused preview. Because each product has 5+ features, use spotlight-plus-grid rather than plain cards. Keep the layout rhythm different between the two blocks: Seedream should feel precision-oriented and image-led; Seedance should feel motion-led with audio-visual synchronization emphasized. Do not make both blocks visually identical.

This section is optional in content depth but should still exist as a concise credibility reinforcement block if needed. Since the content map does not include explicit points, use it as a compact buyer-confidence grid only if there is room; otherwise collapse it into a short operational reassurance strip. Keep it lighter and less prominent than proof and products.

Convert pricing into a decision-oriented comparison block with two product cards. Highlight the video generation plan as the primary commercial anchor because it includes an explicit starting price. Keep the CTA consistent and singular: every button must say 'Get started'. Use solid accent buttons only, no outlines, no gray. Maintain strong contrast and avoid a generic pricing-table look.

There are 5 testimonials, so use a carousel to preserve space and create motion. Prioritize the most relevant creative roles first: Creative Director, Video Producer, Art Director, Marketing Manager, Creative Lead. Keep quote cards dark and premium, with emphasized role labels and minimal decoration. This should feel like practitioner validation, not marketing copy.

End with a focused conversion close. Use a centered or floating card with a short, direct prompt and a single full-width mobile CTA. Keep this as the cleanest section on the page to reduce friction. The CTA button text must still be 'Get started' and remain solid accent at 100% opacity.

blueprint.designPersonality: A dark, production-suite aesthetic for serious visual teams: structured, fast, and enterprise-ready. It feels like a premium AI control room rather than a playful creative tool, with logo-first trust, strong information density, and polished motion-oriented previews.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use dark, high-contrast product visuals: abstract UI shells, layered generation panels, floating media thumbnails, and a second-fold video gallery with autoplay-style preview tiles. Favor PNG UI composites and JPEG cinematic thumbnails; use SVG for all logos and capability icons. Include subtle orange glow edges and performance metric chips rather than colorful gradients.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so it needs a restrained size to preserve hierarchy and prevent awkward wrapping while still feeling authoritative.

colours.colourReason: The palette is derived exclusively from the provided brand colors: orange is the primary brand signal and black/white support the dark premium UI. No unrelated purple, blue, or generic gradient palette is introduced.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column, high-impact hero with logo/brand mark at top, large H1, short supporting paragraph, and a compact trust-badge list; primary conversion action appears immediately in or near the hero area.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top banner hero followed by a lead-capture/form block, then stacked informational product sections; layout favors vertical progression with clear separation between acquisition and detail sections.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily flat utility cards/forms with minimal ornamentation, subtle borders/shadows, rounded corners implied, and strong content grouping; no evidence of glassmorphism or heavy decorative treatments.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One dominant primary CTA in the hero, with section-specific secondary conversion prompts lower on the page; CTAs are direct, action-oriented, and repeated where context changes from awareness to lead capture.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No clear pricing module detected in the reference HTML.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in provided markup; no extractable footer pattern.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Text-led page with logo usage and minimal media presence; no product imagery, video, or media carousel in the visible structure.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked product feature sections with a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and feature list; supports progressive disclosure by separating each product into its own block and allowing feature depth below the headline.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form in its own card immediately after hero, using multiple hidden fields plus visible fields below; designed for qualification and submission rather than checkout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation pattern is visible in the provided HTML; interaction appears static and utility-driven.
designNotes: Structure is optimized for B2B lead generation rather than storytelling.
Content hierarchy is concise and conversion-first, with the hero and form doing most of the work.
Feature presentation is list-based, favoring scanability over rich visual comparison.
The reference emphasizes strong vertical flow and compartmentalized sections instead of complex interactive navigation.
Design system should prioritize clear hierarchy, generous spacing, and reusable content blocks for multi-product pages.

PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

Use dark Theme, add a gallery section in second fold which will contains videos

mustHaveMoments: Brand/logo-led trust strip directly in the hero
Clear product positioning for both Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Primary CTA above the fold with a demo-oriented conversion action
Second-fold video gallery showcasing AI video outputs
Dedicated proof section featuring enterprise credibility and use-case relevance
Product capability sections that separate image generation from video generation
Testimonials from creative and marketing roles
Pricing or quote-request moment for late-stage evaluation
avoidPatterns: Generic AI buzzword-heavy copy without concrete capabilities
Long-form editorial storytelling before proof and product value
Secondary CTAs competing with the main conversion path
Hidden trust signals or badge-only credibility
Dense feature lists without visual examples
Forcing purchase intent when the page goal is evaluation and demo booking
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best positioned as a demo-booking and lead-generation experience for professionals who already understand the category but need confidence in quality, output control, and enterprise readiness. Because the visitor trusts logos most, the design should prioritize a logo-first proof strip and keep trust visible early and often. The dark theme supports a premium, technical, creative-tool feel and helps videos and generated visuals feel more cinematic. A split hero is the strongest fit: one side for high-impact messaging and CTAs, the other for product visuals or motion. Since the second fold must include a gallery section with videos, the page should transition quickly from promise to proof, then into structured product capability sections, testimonials, and quote/demo moments. The overall structure should stay balanced, with enough breathing room for premium perception but enough density to communicate advanced capabilities without wasting scroll depth.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
